# Standing Desk Comparison — Under $300 (Estimated Prices)

> ⚠️ **All prices are approximate and unverified** — based on typical online pricing as of late 2026. Actual prices fluctuate with sales, size choices, and retailers. Check current listings before buying.

---

## 1. Flexispot EC1 (48"×24")

| Spec | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Approx. Price** | ~$250–290 |
| **Height Range** | 28" – 47.6" |
| **Desktop** | 48"×24" (other sizes available at higher cost) |
| **Motor** | Single motor |
| **Weight Capacity** | ~154 lbs |
| **Noise** | ~50 dB (moderate, not disruptive) |
| **Stability** | Good for single-motor; slight wobble at max height |
| **Warranty** | 5-year frame, 2-year motor/electronics |

**Pros:** Trusted brand with strong customer support; solid build for single motor; assembly is straightforward (~30 min); programmable memory handset on most units.  
**Cons:** Single motor means slower lift and marginally less stability at standing height; desktop is on the smaller side; no anti-collision detection.

**Best for:** Someone who wants a proven, no-surprises entry-level desk from a name-brand company and doesn't need a huge work surface.

---

## 2. FEZIBO Dual Motor (48"×24")

| Spec | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Approx. Price** | ~$250–300 |
| **Height Range** | 27.6" – 47.3" |
| **Desktop** | 48"×24" (55"×24" and 63"×24" often available near $300) |
| **Motor** | Dual motor |
| **Weight Capacity** | ~176 lbs |
| **Noise** | ~45 dB (quieter than single-motor competitors) |
| **Stability** | Strong for price; dual-motor crossbar helps lateral stability |
| **Warranty** | 5-year frame, 2-year motor |

**Pros:** Dual motor at this price is the standout feature — faster, smoother, quieter lift; higher weight capacity; anti-collision sensor on many units; good stability even at standing height; multiple color/size combos.  
**Cons:** Brand support is less established than Flexispot; desktop chipboard quality is average; instructions can be slightly confusing.

**Best for:** The value pick — dual-motor performance at single-motor pricing. Ideal for a heavier dual-monitor + laptop setup or anyone who wants smoother height transitions.

---

## 3. VIVO Electric 55" (DESK-V102E / similar)

| Spec | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Approx. Price** | ~$230–280 |
| **Height Range** | 29" – 48" |
| **Desktop** | 55"×24" (wider surface; 60"×24" sometimes in range) |
| **Motor** | Single motor |
| **Weight Capacity** | ~176 lbs |
| **Noise** | ~50–55 dB (average) |
| **Stability** | Decent; wider top helps, but single-motor wobble at max height |
| **Warranty** | 3-year (shorter than competitors) |

**Pros:** Wider desktop for the money — great for dual monitors side-by-side; slightly higher max height (48"); decent weight capacity for a single motor; often the cheapest of the three on sale.  
**Cons:** Shorter warranty; louder motor; stability trails the FEZIBO dual; handset feels cheaper; assembly can be trickier (some report pre-drilled hole misalignment).

**Best for:** Someone who needs a wider work surface on a tight budget and can live with a shorter warranty and average noise.

---

## Quick Verdict

| | Flexispot EC1 | FEZIBO Dual Motor | VIVO 55" |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Best feature** | Brand trust | Dual motor for ~$260 | Wide desktop |
| **Weakness** | Single motor | Weaker brand support | Short warranty |
| **Pick if…** | You want reliability | You want smooth/quiet | You need desk space |

**Overall recommendation:** If prices are close, the **FEZIBO Dual Motor** is the strongest all-around pick — dual motors at this price are hard to beat, and the stability/noise advantage is real. The **Flexispot EC1** is the safe bet if brand reputation and support matter most. The **VIVO** wins only if you specifically need a wider top and every dollar counts.

---
